author.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
author.occupation: German poet, novelist, dramatist and public official
author.biography: Goethe trained in law, became famous while young and spent much of his life in public service at Weimar. He also pursued science and visual art, refusing to make one occupation contain his curiosity. Faust occupied him across decades. Its scholar's dissatisfaction gives that appetite a dangerous form: what happens when knowledge has ceased to satisfy, and the promise of experience seems worth almost any price?

hook.text: What would you trade for the feeling that you are finally alive?

paragraphs: Faust has studied for years and feels that he has missed life itself. Knowledge has brought neither satisfaction nor a secure grasp of what matters. An offer from Mephistopheles turns that dissatisfaction into an experiment.

The promise is experience: to escape the limits of the study and encounter what thinking has failed to supply. It is an exciting promise, especially when weariness makes caution feel like cowardice. But the world contains other people, whose lives cannot be treated as material for one man's awakening.

Goethe moves between argument, song, mockery and scenes of painful intimacy. Mephistopheles is often funny, and his contempt can sound like clarity. Notice whose hopes become disposable when an intelligent person decides that ordinary restraints are beneath him.
What would count as finally having lived? And how would you recognise the point at which the search for a fuller life had begun to empty somebody else's?

orientation.text: This is Part One of Faust, a dramatic poem with changing forms and settings. The opening moves through several frames before we meet Faust in his study.
